text:
lucas: Heads up — noticed sustained memory growth in KV residency for tenant `acme-pro` during our longctx soak. resident pages climbed from ~120k to ~210k over ~6h on a single GPU. fragmentation reported ~42%. not a single big spike, just steady climb.

maria.dev: ugh. any repro or traces? can you paste pprof/heap and a flamegraph?

lucas: attaching quick heap snapshot and a tiny log snippet:
```
# kv residency snapshot
timestamp: 2026-03-12T03:12:00Z
tenant: acme-pro
resident_pages: 210_432
avg_page_size: 8KB
fragmentation_percent: 42
hot_set_ratio: 0.65
```

log tail: `evict_scan found 0 reclaimable pages after 3 scans; tenant_quota=200k pages; soft_watermark=180k`

kv-bot: ALERT: tenant acme-pro crossed soft_watermark (183k) at 2026-03-12T02:51:05Z; automatic throttle not triggered (policy=soft-only). :warning:

samir: grabbed pprof heap + a flamegraph. main finding: many small allocations pinned in `kv/buffer.go:Reserve()` and `kv/page.go:appendFragment()`; fragmentation correlated with repeated partial-page appends during longctx streaming. link: https://internal/fg/pprof/1935012345/heap (flamegraph)

devon: interesting — this looks like reuse failure rather than pure quota overflow. longctx sessions keep appending small deltas, leaving many underfilled pages. when kernel selection switched to the new quant kernels two weeks ago, page-alignment moved from 4KB->8KB which doubled the visible fragmentation per partial-page.

jen: quick mitigation we can try in prod canary: prefer in-place append if remaining_capacity_on_page >= requested_size OR coalesce small fragments when eviction pressure low. pseudo:
```
if page.free_space >= req.len {
  page.append(req)
} else if tenant.reclaimed_fragments >= min_frag && eviction_pressure < P2 {
  coalesce_fragments(page)
  page.append(req)
} else {
  allocate_new_page()
}
```

lucas: repro command I used: `./devtools/kv_repro --tenant acme-pro --longctx --duration 6h --stream-rate 1r/s --avg-chunk 512B` produced the same trend locally. attaching small CSV of resident_pages over time.

maria.dev: thanks. can you also run `go test -run TestEvictPolicy -bench . -memprofile=mem.out` and upload mem.out? I want to see what holds refs to fragments.

samir: did a quick grep on our telemetry: tenants with longctx enabled + high chunking skew show 3x greater resident-to-active ratio. per-tenant quotas are set as hard limits but our soft_watermark is too high and we only do non-disruptive throttles. suggests we need earlier tenant-level eviction or tenant-aware compaction.

devon: proposal: add a per-tenant compaction pass that triggers when fragmentation_percent > 30% AND resident_pages > soft_watermark - 10k. compaction should be bounded (rate-limited) and prefer low-latency windows. Also consider lowering soft_watermark for longctx tenants.

jen: note: compaction is costly on GPU mem copy — implement incremental compaction: move a few pages per second and update residency atomically. algorithm sketch: mark, copy, swap pointers, free old page. rate-limit via credit bucket.

lucas: small perf regression note — after kernel switch, KV page size increased and our `evict_scan` step cost went up by ~15% (more pages to inspect). that may have slowed eviction response and allowed accumulation.

maria.dev: action items?
- lucas: attach mem.out + CSV (by EOD)
- samir: run cluster-wide telemetry query for fragmentation vs longctx flag (tomorrow AM)
- devon: prototype tenant compaction rate-limiter (POC branch)
- jen: write bounded in-place coalescing change and safety checks (review w/ perf)
- qa-ana: schedule canary on dedicated pool once POC ready

qa-ana: will also add a regression test that simulates repeated small appends under longctx and checks resident_pages delta < X after 1h.

lucas: temporary quickfix i'd like to try tonight: lower soft_watermark for tenants with longctx=true by 20%. anyone object?

devon: +1 from me. prefer explicit rollout to small subset then measure.

maria.dev: +1. also add a metric `tenant.compaction_inflight` so we can alert when compaction is active.

samir: will prepare a short note about kernel-selection impacts on page sizing for the infra list — important to correlate model/runtime config changes with memory heuristics.

lucas: thanks all. I'll upload artifacts and start the soft_watermark canary. ping me if you want to pair on the repro. :rocket:
